feedback_interpretation: The authoritative state is 877 observed records and 2,453 eligible candidates. H33 is revised: m209's exceptional 2/1 onset does not transfer to 150 ul, whose measured 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1 sequence is 5.40/9.05, 5.89/11.18 and 7.45/17.05 ml. This rejects propagation of the isolated onset elevation across loading; the original 100 ul input remains unreplicated. Its fixed-100 ul continuation reaches 18.81/51.67 ml at 20/1. H35's long pure-EA completion and initial-decrease alternatives are rejected: m156 completion increases from 8.73 through 9.80, 12.83 and 14.10 to 23.25 ml, while onset decreases between 20/1 and 50/1. Thus broad endpoint monotonicity is still unwarranted. H36 is differentiated: m171 onset stays near 5.7–6.2 ml from 2/1 through 20/1, whereas m172 onset rises to 9.05 ml at 20/1. H37 supports distinct aldehyde slopes: m184 changes by -0.90/+3.09 ml between 2/1 and 10/1, while m185 changes by +2.89/+6.29 ml. H39's predicted large m8 onset rise is rejected by the shallow measured curve; m158 also retains early onset with modest completion variation. H32's sampled m73 completion minimum is located at 1/1: completion is 13.62/10.59/11.60/13.55/15.69 ml across pure EA, 1/1, 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 at density 1.0491 and 100 ul. Persistence remains untested. H27's immediate higher-ratio question is answered: m87's 50-to-100 ul change at 50/1 is -2.92/-0.23 ml, separating onset loading response from nearly unchanged completion. H30 retains joint m162 growth across loading, with 2/1-to-10/1 increments of +6.33/+10.37 ml at 50 ul and +5.24/+9.30 ml at 150 ul; exact slope invariance is unsupported. Recent m55/m56 measurements also support modest benzoate progression. H34 remains rejected because its supposed repeat pair contains different molecules. Earlier m75 and m32 repeats continue to weaken stable loading-step and completion-maximum interpretations. Exceptional m177, m120 and m207 inputs and the isolated m117 near-reversal remain unresolved. The current m18 prediction reversal has reappeared in this packet and supersedes the older ordered-prediction summary, but supplies no measured evidence. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over their measured ranges. All residuals discussed are historical premeasurement errors; selected candidates remain predictions only.
batch_rationale: The latest feedback substantially answers the previous m156, m209 loading-transfer, m73 interior, m87 higher-ratio, m171/m172, m184/m185 and m8/m158 questions. Their findings now motivate transfer tests in less sampled environments. The m27 and m170 sequences compare carbonyl contexts through controlled curves; m51 and m203 test tertiary-alcohol transfer; m6 and m71 extend carbonyl-free oxygen/sulfur coverage. The m188/m192 curves test limits of the newly established aldehyde divergence. Independently selected m74/m91 measurements address a consequential gap between shallow malonate behavior and larger diester responses. Every group supplies interpretable slopes or loading bridges rather than isolated molecular offsets.

m156 completion increases from 8.73 to 9.80, 12.83, 14.10 and 23.25 ml across pure EA, 1/1, 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1 at 50 ul. The predicted long pure-EA completion and initial completion decrease are rejected. The onset decreases from 10.16 at 20/1 to 7.19 at 50/1.

m87 at 50/1 gives 24.51/49.53 ml at 50 ul and 21.59/49.30 ml at 100 ul, so completion is nearly unchanged while onset advances at the higher loading. At 2/1, completion remains strongly later only at the 150 ul corner.

m73 at matched 100 ul and density 1.0491 has completion 13.62/10.59/11.60/13.55/15.69 ml from pure EA through 1/1, 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1, while onset rises. The minimum is sampled at 1/1, and persistence remains untested.
m171 retains shallow onset through 20/1 at 100 ul, whereas m172 develops clearer onset growth between 10/1 and 20/1. Benzyl substitution therefore does not define one transferable response.
At fixed 100 ul, m184 changes from 5.94/10.71 to 5.04/13.80 ml between 2/1 and 10/1, while m185 changes from 5.07/12.36 to 7.97/18.65 ml. Halogenated aldehyde response remains structure-specific.
m8 remains shallow through 10/1 at 50 ul, while m158 remains comparatively shallow in onset with modest completion variation. The predicted strong m8 onset rise is rejected.
m162's 2/1-to-10/1 joint growth is similar at 50 and 150 ul, with small endpoint offsets. This supports conditional transfer of its curve while rejecting a universal loading correction.

The corrected row mapping remains essential: 8fa8d7ec035c6a829dc4 is m156, while fe212637596386c24049 is m163. They are different molecules and conditions; no m163 repeatability conclusion follows from that pair.

Observed 8fa8d7ec035c6a829dc4 is m156 at 50/1 and measures 7.19/23.25 ml; observed fe212637596386c24049 is m163 at 50/1 and measures 24.86/44.05 ml. H34 therefore has no valid identical-input m163 repeat interpretation. This weakens transfer of the exceptional onset but cannot establish its repeatability. m87 completion is close for 50 and 100 ul at 2/1 and 20/1 but later at the 150 ul 2/1 corner, so a global loading correction is unsupported. m162 shows intermediate joint growth at fixed 50 ul; m130 remains modest through 20/1. m75 and m32 repeated inputs disagree enough to weaken deterministic interpretations of isolated loading steps and completion maxima. ml_memo.possible_model_blind_spots: OBSERVED-BASED INFERENCE: Misassigned molecule-condition anchors can manufacture false replication failures and false response curves. CONDITION BLIND SPOT: independent endpoint fits and molecular offsets do not capture nonlinear interactions among ratio, sample volume, loading mass, loading solvent and plug volume. DATA-QUALITY BLIND SPOT: exact-input differences in m75, m32 and m92 are evidence of possible run or integration variability, but do not define a general noise distribution. CHEMICAL PRIOR: silica adsorption, hydrogen bonding, focusing, solubility and injection-zone effects may matter, but none is mechanistically established by the labels. MODEL DIAGNOSTIC: candidate quantile widths, novelty, similarity and extreme predicted volumes are not calibrated uncertainty or acquisition value. Endpoint ordering should be monitored, while V2 minus V1 remains an elution interval rather than uncertainty.
ml_memo.important_model_behaviors: The model often predicts onset reasonably while missing completion growth, but polar and tail examples also show the reverse. Measured m156 and m73 responses demonstrate local reversals, so monotonicity should not be imposed broadly. Loading effects are molecule-, ratio- and endpoint-specific: m87, m162, m200 and m75 do not support a universal loading offset. Historical residual signs change across related donors, acceptors, nitriles, ketones, esters and alcohols; a shared functional-group correction is unlikely to transfer. The current candidate pool also contains model-consistency diagnostics such as predicted V2 below V1; these are predictions only and require a concrete calibration question before being treated as informative.
ml_memo.possible_learning_bottlenecks: The main bottlenecks are conditional interaction representation, V2 tail calibration, and distinguishing learnable response structure from omitted experimental variation. Adaptive sampling has already substantially mapped m54/m175, m53/m59, m73, m156, m167, m173, m125 and much of m162/m163. Further value should come from specific missing contrasts or representative ordinary Row chemistry. Replicates can test persistence of a measured association, but a single repeat cannot identify a noise model or determine which label is correct.
ml_memo.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: The legal pool contains many near-duplicate condition rows and some exact molecule-plus-five-condition duplicates. Deduplication must use molecule identity and all five condition columns, including density and loading-solvent volume. Recent adaptive work is concentrated in a limited set of molecules and high-error tails; moderate common-condition rows and less sampled ester, ether, weak-interaction aromatic, aldehyde and ordinary ketone families remain useful for Row-distribution coverage. Density values such as 1.049 and 1.0491 are distinct represented inputs and should remain distinct in analysis.

ml_memo.recommended_followup_queries: For a future measured round, first verify molecule and condition alignment, then compare V1 and V2 residuals separately. Prioritize contrasts that distinguish ratio slope, loading response and molecular offset within the same molecule or a tightly linked structural pair. Treat exceptional singletons such as m209 2/1 at 100 ul, m177 tail inputs, and m120/m207 loading anomalies as local labels until matched persistence is demonstrated. Reassess Row coverage after removing redundant candidates and before extending already mapped response grids.

hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m51 develop strong joint growth across 1/1-to-10/1 at 150 ul, and does m203 remain modest or begin a later rise?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl-free ring environments require differentiated response curves. Shallow measured m8 and m158 behavior does not establish the intermediate progression of fused-acetal m6 or long-chain substituted thiophene m71.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These curves extend oxygen and sulfur representation while testing whether completion changes independently of onset at ordinary endpoint scales.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m6 completion grow with persistently shallow onset, and where does m71 develop completion growth around its measured 5/1 input?

hypotheses.content: Halogenated aldehydes have differentiated endpoint slopes: m184 completion grows with slightly decreasing onset between 2/1 and 10/1, whereas m185 grows jointly. This does not determine m188 or m192, whose injection contexts also differ.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two independently controlled positional-isomer curves can improve aldehyde transfer without encoding an unsupported halogen-position correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m188 at 150 ul and m192 at 100 ul preserve shallow onset through 20/1, develop joint growth, or differ in their transition locations?

hypotheses.content: Diester membership does not determine a common ratio response. m80 remains near 7.5 ml completion through 20/1, m74 reaches substantially larger higher-ratio endpoints, and m91 has modest measured 10/1 endpoints under another loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected bromomalonate and acetylenic-diester curves test structural limits of polycarbonyl transfer and distinguish onset growth from completion shoulders.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 100 ul, where does m74 begin growing toward its measured 20/1 and 50/1 endpoints, and does m91 remain modest or develop completion recovery by 20/1?

selected_plan.batch_rationale: The latest feedback substantially answers the previous m156, m209 loading-transfer, m73 interior, m87 higher-ratio, m171/m172, m184/m185 and m8/m158 questions. Their findings now motivate transfer tests in less sampled environments. The m27 and m170 sequences compare carbonyl contexts through controlled curves; m51 and m203 test tertiary-alcohol transfer; m6 and m71 extend carbonyl-free oxygen/sulfur coverage. The m188/m192 curves test limits of the newly established aldehyde divergence. Independently selected m74/m91 measurements address a consequential gap between shallow malonate behavior and larger diester responses. selected_plan.expected_learning_value: Expected benefits are improved representation of separate onset and completion slopes, conditional loading transfer and structural limits across ten molecular environments. The batch includes modest-response chemistry where evidence for local invariance would be useful, alongside alcohol and diester conditions that can locate stronger growth. Its connected measurements should constrain transfer beyond the repeatedly investigated adaptive surfaces. Overall Row weighting and a retrained evaluation are not supplied, so no numerical accuracy gain is claimed.
selected_plan.feedback_interpretation: The authoritative state is 877 observed records and 2,453 eligible candidates. This rejects propagation of the isolated onset elevation across loading; the original 100 ul input remains unreplicated. Its fixed-100 ul continuation reaches 18.81/51.67 ml at 20/1. H35's long pure-EA completion and initial-decrease alternatives are rejected: m156 completion increases from 8.73 through 9.80, 12.83 and 14.10 to 23.25 ml, while onset decreases between 20/1 and 50/1. Thus broad endpoint monotonicity is still unwarranted. H36 is differentiated: m171 onset stays near 5.7–6.2 ml from 2/1 through 20/1, whereas m172 onset rises to 9.05 ml at 20/1. H37 supports distinct aldehyde slopes: m184 changes by -0.90/+3.09 ml between 2/1 and 10/1, while m185 changes by +2.89/+6.29 ml. H39's predicted large m8 onset rise is rejected by the shallow measured curve; m158 also retains early onset with modest completion variation. H32's sampled m73 completion minimum is located at 1/1: completion is 13.62/10.59/11.60/13.55/15.69 ml across pure EA, 1/1, 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 at density 1.0491 and 100 ul. Persistence remains untested. H27's immediate higher-ratio question is answered: m87's 50-to-100 ul change at 50/1 is -2.92/-0.23 ml, separating onset loading response from nearly unchanged completion. H30 retains joint m162 growth across loading, with 2/1-to-10/1 increments of +6.33/+10.37 ml at 50 ul and +5.24/+9.30 ml at 150 ul; exact slope invariance is unsupported. Recent m55/m56 measurements also support modest benzoate progression. H34 remains rejected because its supposed repeat pair contains different molecules. Earlier m75 and m32 repeats continue to weaken stable loading-step and completion-maximum interpretations. Exceptional m177, m120 and m207 inputs and the isolated m117 near-reversal remain unresolved. The current m18 prediction reversal has reappeared in this packet and supersedes the older ordered-prediction summary, but supplies no measured evidence. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over their measured ranges. All residuals discussed are historical premeasurement errors; selected candidates remain predictions only.
